records.region: Southwestern Alaska; Dall Lake and Kinia River near Chefornak
records.material_pending_reason: The northeastern opening-to-lake connection and northwest wetland transfer into the westward channel remain unestablished. The downstream Dall Lake–Kinia passage and coastal mouth are supported.
records.geographic_disambiguation: Kinia River identifies the mapped receiving waters across the Dall Lake outlet and lower river past Chefornak. Urrsukvaaq is the local name paired with Kinia River in the community energy-project presentation. Neither is assigned to every upstream selected part.
records.completion_scope: All of FID2723 and its 33 stored parts were considered against five original USGSTopo views. Dall Lake through-passage, the Kinia outlet, Keguk junction, lower river and actual coastal terminal are supported. The chosen northeastern opening and upper northwest/westward wetland transfer are not fully established. This is one material-pending record, not a completed naming-scope hold or a second access-pending record.
records.supported_name_scope: Direct USGSTopo labels support the lower Kinia River component; the named Dall Lake remains a separate lake component. Chukwugwalilik River is an upper-area mapped river, not proof of the selected cross-wetland transfer.

scope_limits: The full selected upper route is not proved; Kinia River is retained only within its supported downstream scope.
Urrsukvaaq is transcribed from community-authored primary usage, without a formal registry or spelling-standard determination.
No modern channel-bank survey, current tidal/flow direction, navigability or operating-condition claim is made.
Chukwugwalilik River is mapped nearby in the upper area; that name is not assigned to an unsupported selected connection.

records.region: Ocampo, Coahuila de Zaragoza, Mexico; mountain and alluvial-plain corridor in the wider El Guaje setting.
records.material_pending_reason: The selected southeastern gully opening, central alluvial-plain through-link and final channel-to-waterbody relation are not established; regional El Guaje naming does not resolve them.
records.geographic_disambiguation: No name is supported for the complete selected river group. El Guaje is independently supported regional lake/plain context and is not promoted to the name of the river or to a verified selected terminal.
records.completion_scope: All 37 stored parts were considered against municipal terrain/cartography and regional prose, but the selected opening, central through-link and terminal correspondence remain incomplete.
records.supported_name_scope: No name is supported for the complete selected river group. El Guaje is independently supported regional lake/plain context and is not promoted to the name of the river or to a verified selected terminal.

scope_limits: The selected southeastern opening and central alluvial connection have not been followed continuously on independently read material.
The northern valley has mapped channels and side approaches, but the selected complete joining chain and actual terminal relation remain unresolved.
El Guaje is a lake, plain, subbasin and priority-region name in the inspected context; none of those meanings proves the name of this full selected river.
Municipal map and biodiversity-project dates are historical source context, not observations of current wetness, banks, flow permanence, salinity or reservoir operations.
No formal registry confirmation or product naming change is claimed.

records.material_pending_reason: The chosen northern opening and its upper Negro connection remain outside usable source-map coverage. Lower Negro–Peulla, the full Todos Los Santos lake passage and the Petrohué–Ralún/Reloncaví terminal are supported.
records.geographic_disambiguation: Provisional representative-system candidate only. Primary sources distinguish the upstream Río Negro, Lago Todos Los Santos and downstream Río Petrohué; the unresolved chosen opening prevents confirming the complete selected system.
records.completion_scope: Both mainstem fragments and all 66 parts considered; the opening and upper Negro approach remain incomplete, while the lake join, outflow, lower river and actual estuary-head terminal are supported.
records.supported_name_scope: Provisional representative-system candidate only. Primary sources distinguish the upstream Río Negro, Lago Todos Los Santos and downstream Río Petrohué; the unresolved chosen opening prevents confirming the complete selected system.

scope_limits: The remaining material gap is a continuous primary-source correspondence from the exact selected northern opening through the upper Negro corridor to the visible lower river. The inferred regional Negro setting does not fill this gap.
Río Petrohué is supported for the downstream named river and as a provisional representative-system candidate, not as a scalar name for the Negro reach or the lake.
Peulla is a distinct tributary/junction name in the consulted material. No unselected Peulla headwater or other tributary is added to the selected scope.
No independently selected glacial, reservoir or managed transfer is established in the inspected route; current hydrology, exact banks and official-registry adoption are unverified.

records.candidate_name_role: Provisional representative receiving-system identity; selected headward connection incomplete
records.material_pending_reason: The selected eastern headward feeder and its join to the mapped Tempisquito–Tempisque trunk remain unestablished; the middle and lower corridor, interfragment join and actual inland Palo Verde terminal are supported.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The connected Tempisquito–Tempisque inland corridor and the lower Tempisque passage along Palo Verde are supported. The selected eastern headward spur has not been independently connected to that mapped corridor. Tempisque is not assigned as a scalar name to every upper reach.
records.completion_scope: Bounded source research is finished. Both mainstem fragments, their join, the selected opening, modified middle-river context, lower wetlands and actual terminal were considered. Completion is withheld only for the unestablished selected headward feeder/connection. This is not a demand for exact banks, a precise name-change vertex, contemporary flow or operating status.
records.supported_name_scope: The connected Tempisquito–Tempisque inland corridor and the lower Tempisque passage along Palo Verde are supported. The selected eastern headward spur has not been independently connected to that mapped corridor. Tempisque is not assigned as a scalar name to every upper reach.

scope_limits: The eastern headward opening is an unresolved feeder/connection. No source establishes its relation to the mapped Tempisquito headwater; it is not treated as a mere exact-bank or source-vertex discrepancy.
The supported Tempisque receiving trunk does not justify assigning one scalar hydronym to the whole selected group.
Lower correspondence is regional/corridor-scale. The actual stored terminal is preserved within the inland lower Tempisque, without a surveyed shore, local subreach name or ocean-mouth claim.
The sources document generalized and historical geography. Current water extent, flow, wetland management and operating conditions were not required or assessed.
Inherited publication restrictions were preserved at their exact scopes; no Costa Rican institution-wide ban is inferred.

reconstruction_rule: Start from the pinned r46 cumulative index and apply later append-only deltas in verified commit order, rejecting duplicate IDs. Keep base records, scope clauses, region qualifiers and assessment histories unchanged. Apply explicit status-list changes. Subtract all recorded IDs from the exact eligible initial inventory to recover unrecorded targets; pending IDs remain recorded but are not completed source reviews.
publication_boundary: Own factual name/scope findings, public official URLs, bounded geometry metadata and public continuity pins only. No original maps, crops, complete coordinates or private source/derivative/registration fingerprints. Official hosting does not establish source redistribution rights.

research_order.progress_rule: Follow the actual continental order: Americas, Asia, Africa, Europe, then other, with all rivers before lakes. Preserve original queue IDs and ranks for continuity; apply documented geographic deferrals without counting them as name research, and place deferred objects into their corrected later phase by length-descending, stable-ID order. Prior candidate and scope-held assessments remain unresolved where stated.
